title: Golden Ray — St Simons Sound
short_location: St Simons Sound, Glynn County, Georgia

gallery.blurb: Oil kept flushing out of a shipwreck being cut apart. Who is responsible for a wreck?

notes: PROVISIONAL — NO SAR-VISIBLE SLICK. Fixed-wreck infrastructure case. Oil began flushing from the Golden Ray wreck on 31 Jul 2021 during salvage lifting of Section Six; tidal flows carried it onto St Simons and Jekyll Island beaches and marsh through August. This S1A pass (+9 d) is the closest Sentinel-1 coverage of the sound — S1 only images here on a 12-day ascending repeat. The wreck + salvage cluster (VB-10000 crane barge, containment barrier) is the bright knot at the sound mouth (~-81.40, 31.13). St Simons Sound is enclosed, sheltered, calm water: the weathered sheen does not show in SAR (dB sampling: no coherent VV+VH depression). Pending Akshat's call: run this as trace + attribute + verify seeded from the known wreck position (needs the trace-without-detect contract change), NOT as a detection case. Source: USCG / St Simons Sound Incident Response Unified Command; SkyTruth published (optical) imagery.
